simple.meaning: נִדָּה (niddâh) appears 29 times in the Hebrew Scriptures as a person-name in the Hebrew text. The surrounding account also brings the name into blood crying from the ground.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Leviticus, Numbers, 2 Chronicles, Ezra, Lamentations, and 2 more, beginning at Leviticus 12:2. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as blood, Israel.

simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows נִדָּה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

definitions.full: H5079. niddah נִדָּה noun feminine impurity (as abhorrent, shunned) ; — absolute ׳נ Ezek 18:6 +; construct נִדַּת Lev 12:2 +; suffix נִדָּתָהּ 12:5 +; — impurity (especially P and Ezekiel): 1 of ceremonial impurity , as union with brother's wife, Lev 20:21 ; especially of menstruation Ezek 18:6 (read בְּנִדָּתָהּ אִשָּׁה for ᵑ6 ׳א נִדָּה ᵑ0 Co), הַנּ ׳טְמֵאַת 22:10 , compare 36:17 , דְּוֺתָהּ נִדַּת Lev 12:2 , compare 12:5 ; 15:19-20 , 24 , 25 ( ׳עֶתנִֿדּ ), (3 t. in verse), 15:26 ( נִדּ ׳מִשְׁכַּב ), 15:26 ( נִדּ ׳טֻמְאַת ), 15:33 ; 18:19 ; of defilement contracted by contact with a corpse, (הַ)נִּדָּה מֵי water of impurity (i.e. to remove it, compare Di) Num 19:9 , 13 , 20 , 21 (twice in verse); 31:23 . 2 figurative (with allusion to cerem. usage), impure thing , Ezek 7:19-20 , (of gold), Lam 1:17 (of Jerusalem); of idolatry, immorality, etc., 2Chr 29:5 ; Ezra 9:11 ( נִדָּה אֶרֶץ ), 9:11 , Zech 13:1 ( וּלְנִדָּה לְחַטַּאת ).
